hazards.name: Space radiation
hazards.summary: Radiation is not only stealthy, but considered one of the most hazardous aspects of spaceflight.
hazards.watches: An estimated mission dose against NASA's 600 mSv career limit.

hazards.name: Isolation and confinement
hazards.summary: Behavioral responses occur among groups of people far from Earth who are isolated and confined in a small space over a long period of time.
hazards.watches: Reaction speed and sleep against your own normal.

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.summary: Planning and self-sufficiency will be key to successful deep space missions.
hazards.watches: Steps you can follow without waiting for Earth.

hazards.name: Gravity fields
hazards.summary: On Mars, astronauts would need to live and work in three-eighths of Earth’s gravitational pull for up to two years.
hazards.watches: Blood pressure, including low readings and fainting signs.

hazards.name: Hostile and closed environments
hazards.summary: A spacecraft is not only a home, it’s also a machine.
hazards.watches: Emergency guides for burns and chemical splashes.
